review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the simp sets of `ProjectiveClass` and `K0`. I checked uses of `of_fin_fun_eq_nsmul` and `of_repr` across the formal-frontier sources. I found no loops or competing rules. The `ProjectiveClass` simp set looks coherent: `of_prod`, `of_zero`, `of_ulift`, `of_repr`, and `lift_of` all rewrite toward simpler forms. The one clear gap is on the `K0` side: it mirrors only part of the `ProjectiveClass` simp lemmas. I did not run Lean. I also did not check whether the rewrites in the clients would shrink once the lemmas exist, so the benefit is inferred from the manual workarounds.

findings.declaration: KTheory.K0.of (K0 simp interface: missing K0.of_repr and K0.of_fin_fun_eq_nsmul)
findings.excerpt: noncomputable def of : K0 R := ofClass R (ProjectiveClass.of R M)
findings.problem: `K0.of` is an opaque (non-reducible) def. `K0.of` therefore does not see through to `ProjectiveClass.of`, so simp lemmas stated for `ProjectiveClass.of` do not fire on `K0.of`. `K0` mirrors `of_ulift`, `of_zero` and `of_prod` from `ProjectiveClass`, but not the simp lemma `ProjectiveClass.of_repr` or the simp lemma `ProjectiveClass.of_fin_fun_eq_nsmul`. As a result, `K0.of R (repr M)` and `K0.of R (Fin n → Rᵐᵒᵖ)` have no simp normal form. Downstream code works around this by rewriting `← K0.ofClass_of`, then applying the `ProjectiveClass` lemma, then rewriting `K0.ofClass_of` again. The `ofClass_of` simp lemma points the other way, so simp cannot do this round trip on its own.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem K0.of_repr : of R (ModuleCat.FiniteProjective.repr Rᵐᵒᵖ M) = of R M` and `@[simp] theorem K0.of_fin_fun_eq_nsmul (n : ℕ) : of R (Fin n → Rᵐᵒᵖ) = n • of R Rᵐᵒᵖ`. Prove them in the style of `K0.of_ulift`, i.e. `simp only [of, ProjectiveClass.of_repr]` and `simp only [of, ProjectiveClass.of_fin_fun_eq_nsmul, map_nsmul]`. Both are terminating, shrinking rewrites, and they complete the `K0` mirror of the `ProjectiveClass` normal form.
findings.benefit: `simp` can then normalise K₀ generators of ring-universe representatives and of free modules. The three-step `rw [← K0.ofClass_of, ProjectiveClass.of_fin_fun_eq_nsmul, map_nsmul, K0.ofClass_of]` workarounds in client files can be replaced by one `simp` call, and the K₀ interface matches the class-monoid interface.
